findings.summary: The record-format doc lists the introspection record's later optional fields, but it will not mention the three new lists.
findings.evidence: docs/records.md:166 reads 'An introspection record has two post-mortem additions, both read as absent on older records:' and then documents planning_stopped and jev.context_prevention. Decision 8 skips docs/records.md, so the doc for athena.introspection/1 would leave out three new optional keys. No test enforces this doc; I grepped *.rs for records.md and found only status.rs references to other sections. Fix: Add one bullet to that docs/records.md section. It should name other_causes, open_hypotheses and contradictions, say they are omitted when empty and capped at INTROSPECTION_LIST_CAP, and say that `cause` stays the main cause. Then change 'two post-mortem additions' to match.

findings.summary: The failure path is shown only as clean_texts returning Err. No test shows that the introspection is stored as failed with that reason.
findings.evidence: Criterion 5 says the introspection 'is recorded as failed, with a reason'. Test 5(b) calls clean_texts directly with a failing closure and asserts the Err string. It then claims this is 'the string apply_answer stores in record.failure with status Failed', but nothing asserts on record.failure or status. In apply_answer (introspect.rs:1485-1499) the Err-to-record.failure step is the part that changes. plain_boundary_text (boundary.rs:264-280) has no input known to fail, so the plan's limit is real. Fix: Keep clean_texts. Also add a test that drives the closure-to-record mapping, for example a small private fn that takes the reword closure, is used by apply_answer, and writes record.failure. Assert record.failure == Some("the answer could not be reworded: ...") and that the record is not Recorded. Or say plainly in the test doc and the CHANGELOG that the stored failure is shown only by reading the code.

findings.summary: The request asks for `status: not shown` together with the test that shows it, but the measure names only a filtered cargo command.
findings.evidence: The request says: 'or `status: not shown` and the test that shows it.' The planned measure reads '... (cargo test -p athena-core introspect); status: not shown'. That filter runs dozens of tests and does not single out the one that proves the requirement. Fix: Name the test in the measure, for example `cargo test -p athena-core several_causes_hypotheses_and_contradictions_are_recorded`, and keep the `status: not shown` ending.

summary: I checked the plan against the code in the snapshot and it holds up. IntrospectionRecord (introspection.rs:182) uses deny_unknown_fields, and it already uses the serde default/skip_serializing_if pattern for planning_stopped and jev. So three Vec<String> fields with the same attributes will keep old records parsing with the same bytes. apply_answer (introspect.rs:1479-1499) already runs one redact_all and a plain_boundary_text loop over a `text` vector. Adding the list entries to that vector and splitting them off before the empty-field check, the text[2] gate marking and the text[0]/text[1] comparison at 1575 is correct. Pulling out a clean_texts helper is a reasonable seam. plain_boundary_text (boundary.rs:264-280) does fail after rewording in principle, but the plan is right that no deterministic test input reaches that failure. I grepped `IntrospectionRecord {` and got exactly the 15 full literals the plan lists, plus three helper fns that don't need edits. The edits outside the deliverables are forced by the compiler, and Athena's scope findings are answered by decision 9. The spec measure ends `status: not shown`, which both measure_problem (hestia.rs:1229) and check_how_it_is_met (xtask/tests/spec.rs:194) accept. The sound design points: `cause` stays the hestia grouping key, the lists are capped, and validate is owned by the data crate. I have three minor points. docs/records.md documents introspection record additions and would go stale. The failure half of criterion 5 is shown at the clean_texts level, not on the stored record. The measure names the test command but not a specific test.
